purpose: Settle cancelled camera/sample start calls even when native acquisition or presenter startup remains pending, retaining late-resource cleanup and replacement-session ownership.

contract.completion: Each run owns a cancellation completion. Stop, failure and the unchanged startup deadline release the application start wait with false; successful startup returns true. Cancellation applies both before worker/camera readiness and while awaiting onReady.
contract.ownership: Native getUserMedia and video.play cannot be cancelled by settling the application wait. Their eventual completion/rejection remains observed; late acquired streams stop all tracks, and presenter epoch checks retain replacement ownership. No claim of native cancellation or physical memory bounds across restarts.
contract.verification: Reproduce parent start waits remaining unsettled after Stop with a ready worker and pending acquisition, and with pending video.play. Deterministic unit controls exercise Stop, exact startup timeout, failure, replacement, late success/rejection and synchronous failure. Browser controls hold real fake-camera acquisition or video playback, require application completion before release, and verify cleanup plus replacement sample progress. Retain all existing real WASM/model, geometry, capture/result/progress, CSP and privacy assertions.
contract.preservation: No Rust/core/GPU/dependency change or compilation. Preserve scientific JSON, frozen native outputs, prior camera and renderer evidence, resolved lockfile and release WASM. Reuse installed runtime/browser, matching bindgen and pinned vendor hardlinks.

resources.strategy: Fresh E: site with hash-checked vendor hardlinks and reused release WASM. All local command inputs are source-bound; preserve previous outputs and failures.
resources.asset_download_scope: No new local SDK/model acquisition. Bounded public HTTPS verification streams without retaining vendor payloads.

remaining_80_percent: Canonical calibration/timing, independent real motion, full-room accuracy, qualifying physical Linux hardware and integrated operational acceptance remain open.
